record.original_question: For the Lie groupoid of multiphase or generalized volume-preserving diffeomorphisms, equipped with the source-wise right-invariant L2 metric whose geodesics describe multiphase Euler flows, can one describe its differential geometry, including sectional curvature, Ricci curvature, and conjugate points, analogously to Arnold's geometry of the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group D_mu(M)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian manifold with smooth volume form $\mu$. Consider the Lie groupoid $\mathcal{G}$ of "multiphase" (generalized volume-preserving) diffeomorphisms of $M$: objects are smooth probability densities (or measures) on $M$ absolutely continuous with respect to $\mu$, and morphisms from a density $\rho_0$ to a density $\rho_1$ are smooth diffeomorphisms $\varphi : M \to M$ with $\varphi_* \rho_0 = \rho_1$. Equip $\mathcal{G}$ with the source-wise right-invariant $L^2$ Riemannian metric: at a morphism $\varphi$ with source $\rho_0$, tangent vectors are identified via right translation with vector fields $u$ on $M$, and the inner product is
$$\langle u, v \rangle_{\rho_0} = \int_M \langle u(x), v(x) \rangle_{g(x)} \, \rho_0(x) \, d\mu(x).$$
The geodesics of this metric describe multiphase Euler flows generalizing Arnold's geodesic interpretation of the incompressible Euler equation on the group $D_\mu(M)$ of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms.

Develop the differential geometry of $\mathcal{G}$ with this metric in analogy with Arnold's geometry of $D_\mu(M)$. In particular:
(a) derive a workable formula for the sectional curvature of $\mathcal{G}$ along pairs of tangent directions at a morphism;
(b) define and compute (or estimate the sign of) the Ricci curvature in suitable directions, including the case $M = \mathbb{T}^n$;
(c) determine the existence and distribution of conjugate points along geodesics, relating them to stability/instability of multiphase Euler flows.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open program. Recent work (2025) has computed sectional and Ricci curvatures for measure-preserving diffeomorphism groups on the sphere, non-orientable surfaces, and tori, but a systematic curvature/conjugate point theory for the multiphase (generalized volume-preserving) diffeomorphism groupoid analogous to Arnold's theory does not appear in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Curvatures of Measure-Preserving Diffeomorphism Groups of Non-orientable Surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Computations of sectional and normalized Ricci curvatures for measure-preserving diffeomorphism groups on Klein bottle and RP^2, extending Arnold's program.
status_evidence.claim: Recent extensions of Arnold's curvature program target classical D_mu(M), not the multiphase groupoid.

status_evidence.title: Ricci Curvature for Hydrodynamics on the Sphere
status_evidence.snippet: A notion of Ricci curvature for volume-preserving diffeomorphisms on the 2-sphere is introduced via quantization.
status_evidence.claim: Ricci curvature in this geometric hydrodynamic setting is still being defined and computed for individual manifolds.
